milestones.text: Phase 0: environment checked; 'kodiak' taken everywhere, so kodiak-s1 under grizzlypeaksoftware
Phase 1: architecture approved (packed sequence + structured attention mask)
Phase 2: 20 datasets converted; eval set v0.1 with 24 human-reviewed synthetic examples
Phase 3: bit-identical ModernBERT parity; both overfit tests pass; torch.compile 2x
Track A deferred: Track B trains in an hour, pretraining would take days
First Track B run: early stopping misfired on a 7-example group (fixed)
Preliminary eval: Kodiak ties Qwen 27B in-domain, 400x faster, better calibrated; weaker on new tasks
Local status dashboard added
DigitalOcean inference: key was clipped (68 vs 71 chars), then a billing gate cleared at 10:33
Cloud pilot #1: 26% kept (gpt-oss paraphrased its evidence)
Cloud pilot #2: 88% kept after fixes; $0.73 per 1,000 jobs
Verifier bake-off: DeepSeek V3.2 wins (97% agreement with human review, 0 failures, 10x faster than gpt-oss)
Switched synthetic generation to the cloud: gpt-oss writes, DeepSeek checks (7,700 jobs, ~$8)
Generator v2 design drafted: taxonomy, real-document grounding, hard-example mining, minimal pairs
Generator v2 design approved
Synthetic batch complete: 9,702 examples (3,290 local + 6,412 cloud); cloud cost ~$5.50 + checker
Data scaling test started: 0 vs 3,300 vs 9,411 synthetic examples (same pool)
Scaling test: synthetic data helps overall (+1.2 pts), calibration, and synthetic-style tasks, but NOT held-out tasks (flat), so build better data, not more of the same
Recipe test started: repeat cap (Qasper was seen 23x, prompt-injections 29x), full LR schedule, tuned abstain threshold
Recipe test: repeat cap lifts held-out accuracy 62.5% -> 66.4% (jailbreak +8.8) for -1.6 in-domain; cap + full schedule become defaults
Generator v2.0 built: taxonomy of 16 sectors / 320 domains / 971 document types, ~45% real FineWeb passages, inference questions, MinHash dedupe, budget cap (11 tests)
v2 pilots ($0.15): removing 'unknown' options + reader-style questions on real text cut checker disagreement (inferred 37% -> 20%, stated 8% -> 2%)
55 v2 eval candidates (165 questions) ready for Shane's review in tools/review.html
Shane's review of v2 eval candidates: 92.7% (unanswerable 100%); added one-defensible-answer rules + two critics; 11k-job batch launched (cap $30)
Strategy adopted (D27, docs/STRATEGY.md): frontier-class open-weights decision model, with a release bar written before measuring; open zero-shot classifiers added as baselines
Open-classifier baselines: Kodiak far ahead overall (+23 pts acc), best calibration, fastest; but GLiClass-instruct-large edges it on held-out (0.705 vs 0.691 forced). Best-in-class bar not met yet
First upload: best model (R1) as a PRIVATE preview at huggingface.co/cortex-agent-llc/kodiak-small-r1-preview (weights verified by SHA-256); public release after the v2 A/B + release kit
Release kit: Kodiak.from_pretrained loader, export/push CLI, [infer] install extra, model card draft, quickstart; calibration-bug fix re-pushed to the private preview; CPU ~80 ms
Distribution plan: demo Space + Inference Endpoints handler built and tested; hosted Kodiak API by Cortex Agent chosen as the productization path
GitHub repo made public (building in public); weights stay private until the v2 A/B picks the launch model
Demo Space running (private): comgen42/kodiak-demo loads the private model from cortex-agent-llc; ~0.85 s round trip; transfer to the org and go public at launch
Research preview public: cortex-agent-llc/kodiak-small-r1-preview (weights, handler, preview model card); demo Space gets a preview banner
v2.0 batch done: 9,428 kept examples for $25.38 (Stage 2 goal met)
A/B with 3 seeds each: v2.0 cuts wrong refusals ~60%, abstain precision 0.84→0.92, better calibration; never-seen forced accuracy unchanged (0.72 vs 0.72). The single-run '+5–7 pts' was noise
Research preview v2 public: cortex-agent-llc/kodiak-small-v2-preview (seed chosen on validation); demo switched to v2; r1 card points to v2. Honest note: the crushed-box fix is fragile
Eval set v0.2 frozen: +8 never-seen sources (legal, moral, finance, science, clickbait score, poetry); held-out 4 → 12 tasks, 1,000 → 4,200 examples
Stage 3 paused after 5 pilots ($0.54): blind AI raters disagree on most judgment ratings (58–82%), so the labels are too noisy to teach; next: large-model results, then try low/medium/high bands

Outside validation: CMU 'JEV-as-a-Judge' (arXiv:2609.26550) confirms the accept-confident/escalate-unsure cascade; OpenRouter launches jev-router. Backlog ranked: Kodiak-as-a-judge demo (+ public benchmark), Kodiak Router, Zork
Zork showdown published (Shane): 0 invalid moves in ~20k, but Jev beat Kodiak, and v2 was confidently wrong on game states. Calibration doesn't survive distribution shift (D32)

ModernBERT-large (3 seeds) beats every open zero-shot classifier on eval v0.2 never-seen tasks: 60.9% vs 57.9% best clean rival. Release criterion 1 met by large (D33); ratings and off-distribution calibration still weak
Ensemble of 3 large runs: never-seen forced 62.3%, calibration error 0.099 (from ~0.128), abstain precision 93% (D34). Next: distill the ensemble into one model
Kodiak large v2 research preview public (cortex-agent-llc/kodiak-large-v2-preview, weights verified); demo gets a small/large picker and a 'Categorize a list' tab
Phase 6: ONNX export + Node.js/Docker server (D35); model.onnx published in both preview repos
Distillation of the large ensemble into small: no gain, calibration slightly worse (D36, negative result)
Polarity batch (mixed/neutral tone): 3,894 examples for $9.78; 3-seed test queued
Release criterion 2 met narrowly: Qwen3-8B leads by 7.9 on never-seen tasks (world knowledge); Kodiak→LLM cascade beats both (0.740 vs 0.709 with 43% escalated) (D37)
Generator v2.1 hard-example mining tied random selection (3 seeds each): not adopted (D41). A demo user found a label-word overlap shortcut (0.97 → 0.48 on a reworded ticket): v2.2's first target
Calibration batch (unfamiliar inputs) had no effect, 3 seeds (D42): the fourth flat data tweak in a row; small-model data tweaks stop here. Demo gets a 'Did Kodiak get something wrong?' form
Demo: 'Returns Desk: you vs. the Bear' game (233 computed-answer cases) and a live feedback form feeding a private review dataset
Returns Desk simulator data (computed labels, $2.01): word-trap probe 3 → 5 of 8, the first targeted data gain since v2.0; costs ~1 pt and teaches a new shortcut (D43)
Returns Desk v2 (three worlds, $1.21) matched v1: probe gain real but unreliable across seeds, same ~1-pt cost; simulators move to v0.2 (D44). Book proposal drafted
Accuracy mode published (3-run large ensemble, threshold from a validation rule fixed in advance): never-seen 0.623, abstain precision 0.94, ECE 0.059 (D45). Fine-tuning kit built: demo 75.8% → 98.3%
Ettin-1B (E15) clears its pre-set bar: never-seen 0.666 vs 0.629 bar (large 0.609, Qwen3-8B 0.688); guard miss on 'can't tell' precision (0.86); 2 confirming seeds running (D46)
Ettin-1B confirmed on 3 seeds: never-seen 0.659 ± 0.013 vs large 0.609 (+5.0); gap to Qwen3-8B now ~3 points; 'can't tell' precision 0.87 still below 0.90 (D47)

1B accuracy mode (E16) missed its precision target (0.879 < 0.90) despite the best calibration yet; single 1B published as kodiak-xl-v2-preview (D48). Demo redesigned: answer cards with confidence bars
Decision Index run 1: 12.75 (below the pre-set 15-25); diagnosed an empty-state format mismatch (35% of requests); fixed with one declared rule, validated on our data; run 2 launched (D50)
Decision Index run 2: Kodiak XL 17.19, rank #48 of 71, 5th among ≤2B models (pre-set expectation 15-25); report card sets the next data targets (D51)
E17 seed 1: skills score 0.518 → 0.980 with every guard holding; abstain precision 0.891 and probe 6/8 (D52). Confirming seeds started.
E17 confirmed over 3 seeds: four new skills (0.518 → 0.981) at no general cost; kept (D53). Seed 1's precision/probe bonus was noise.
Release naming decided: Kodiak-v0.2-<size> (150M / 400M / 1B), no 'preview' (D54). Decision Index re-run with the E17 model started.
Decision Index with the E17 model: 17.57 (was 17.19). Skills transfer to real data (ESCI, HoVer, BFCL +12-18 pts); some classification regressions; not submitted (D55).
Decision Index diagnosis (D56): E17's gains are real across 3 seeds; the 'regressions' were XL v2 seed-1 luck, except a phishing wording fragility.
E18 (option-wording robustness) approved; checker-verified rewordings for 279 training labels and 114 eval labels (~$0.05).
E18 (reworded options) missed its bar: consistency 0.621 → 0.678 (needed 0.721). One-seed side effect: never-seen 0.680, better calibration (D57).
E19: reworded options confirmed over 3 seeds: never-seen 0.662 → 0.689 and calibration error 0.109 → 0.085 (D58). Biggest gain since the 1B backbone; joins the v0.2 recipe.
Shane: ship v0.2. Kodiak-v0.2-1B = E17 skills + reworded options, seed 1 (picked on validation); accuracy mode = 3 models. Wording trap moves to v0.3.
v0.2 released: Kodiak-v0.2-1B is live on Hugging Face; the demo runs on ZeroGPU with v0.2 as the default (D59). Accuracy mode uploading.
Accuracy mode published (weights verified) and added to the ZeroGPU demo. Both v0.2 models are live.
v0.2 announcement published on cortexagent.com (the site's first post).
Ranking (aurc_gap_closed) added as a metric and guard after a Hugging Face reviewer's analysis; model cards updated (D60). E20 code ready.
Skills roadmap: 12 candidate decision kinds screened on v0.2 ($0.35). Clear gaps: pairwise judge, sarcasm, policy violation. Decision-kinds tracker added to the Research tab.
Decision Index, v0.2 accuracy mode: 18.69 (from 17.19); 4th among ≤2B models on the last board seen. Not submitted (D61).
Submitted Kodiak-v0.2-1B accuracy mode (18.69) to the Decision Index: PR #49.
E20 (wording-consistency loss) approved; full run resumed from step 517.
E20 (wording-consistency loss) killed: agreement learned on training wordings didn't transfer (D62). v0.2 stays the best model.
E21 skills-2 batch done: 23,118 checked examples for $11.94; E21 training started.
E21 seed 1: skills-2 0.142 → 0.950 and real MT-Bench judgments +0.04 → +0.28; two guards missed by seed-noise margins; decision pending (D63).
Shane chose option B for E21: two confirming seeds, guards judged on 3-seed means (rule written before they ran).
E21 confirmation: skills learned on all 3 seeds (0.959; MT-Bench +0.31) but killed by its pre-written rule on the wording-trap probe (4.7 < 5) (D64).
D65: six rules against folly experiments; a 100-item trap test shows E21 improves the wording trap (0.867 → 0.913), so the 8-sentence probe that killed it was misleading.
Shane: don't ship E21; its skills data carries forward. GOAL.md guards now come from docs/NOISE.md (D65).
Screening 2 (20 kinds, $0.6) + real-data probes: RAGBench +0.14 and SemEval stance +0.24 are real gaps; E22 proposed (target on real data).
E22 batch done: 19,664 checked examples for $13.87; seed 1 training started.
E22 KEEP (D66): seven new decision kinds; real-data decisions 0.211 → 0.358 across 3 seeds; abstain precision 0.931. v0.3 candidate.
Shane: release v0.3 (E22 recipe). Single model = seed 1 by validation loss.
Shane: skip Decision Index runs for upcoming models; resubmit once the model is dialed in.
Kodiak-v0.3-1B published (weights verified); demo switched to v0.3.
v0.3 released: both models public (weights verified) and in the ZeroGPU demo.
Outside feedback (D67): step safety is keyword-level; cards corrected; rule 7 adds contrastive tests and a flip-rate guard; word-matching traced to public intent data.
Contrastive eval v0.1 (rule 7): policy violation is a real skill (pair acc 0.567); refund (0.220) and step safety (0.053) are shortcuts. ~$0.52.

Word-counter check: a bag-of-words model reading one field passes our step-safety (0.94) and refund (0.95) tests; contrastive pairs catch it (pair acc ~0). New free pre-batch check: scripts/shortcut_check.py.
E23 pilot passed ($0.10): contrast groups drop the one-field word-counter from 0.76-0.91 to 0.31-0.58.
Contrastive test v0.2 (DeepSeek-written, 198 pairs, $0.54). v0.3 baseline for E23, both tests pooled: pair accuracy 0.302 ± 0.017 (3 seeds).
D68: rule 6 is now a time box per problem plus both outcomes written before each run; proposal log on the Research tab.
Release audit (D69) on v0.3: confirms step safety ignores the task (4%) with no new data; finds pairwise position bias (26%), tool list ignored (4%), three synthetic tests too weak. Red team $0.12.
Contrast-group batch done: $8.46, 6,889 step-safety + 9,449 refund examples (E23 uses 2,500 each; rest banked).
E23 KEEP (D71): contrastive pair accuracy 0.302 → 0.566 over 3 seeds; all guards hold (never-seen 0.691). Refund a real fix; step safety partly hedge words (D70).
E24 pilot passed ($0.37): cue-balanced groups remove the hedge-word cues; refund changed-words reader 0.80 → 0.51.
Contrastive v0.3 ($2.07): 182 cue-hard pairs. Baseline: v0.3 0.231, E23 0.363 ± 0.033 (3 seeds).
E24 cue-balanced batch done: $8.56 (1,278 step-safety + 1,356 refund groups kept). E24 seed 1 training from 18:51.
Decision Index listing (D72): v0.2 accuracy mode full score 11.8, =96 of 115. Public part 19.1 matches our 18.69; new-domain tasks score 0.9.
E24 KEEP (D73): refund fixed (cue-hard pairs 0.378 → 0.576, 3 seeds), all guards hold. Step safety not fixed by synthetic data: parked. E24 = v0.4 candidate.
Model check (D74): on 3,550 never-seen questions Kodiak 0.676 vs untrained Qwen3-1.7B 0.572 and 0.6B 0.455; Kodiak also ahead on all four real-data tests.
v0.4 release candidate built: E24 seed 1 + accuracy mode; release audit run; cards drafted for Shane.

ideas.name: Next big question: task variety (FLAN-style) vs an LLM backbone
ideas.why: Model check: untrained Qwen3-1.7B 0.572 vs Kodiak 0.676 on never-seen, so the encoder isn't the obvious ceiling. Next: a task-variety curve (15 / 30 / 100+ distinct tasks at the same example count), and maybe fine-tune a 1.7B LLM on our data as the definitive backbone test.

ideas.name: 📌 Hedge-word shortcut in contrast groups (outside feedback, D70)
ideas.status: confirmed for step safety; refund is a real fix
ideas.why: Diff reader (changed words only): 'but' marks 'ask first' in 98% of training groups. E23's step-safety gain is mostly on pairs cue words can solve (v0.2: 0.36 → 0.73) vs 0.15 → 0.27 on the rest; refund gains more on the pairs cue words can't solve (0.34 → 0.60). Fix next: cue-balanced groups + a diff-reader check on pilots and tests; contrastive v0.3 with 'never' balanced (now 7 of 200 sides).

ideas.name: Release audit findings (v0.3) to fix next
ideas.why: Pairwise judge position bias on real data (26% of answers move when answers swap); tools ignores the tool list (4%); long-hallucination synthetic test is ~87% one answer (useless); sarcasm and stance synthetic tests passable by a word-counter (1.00); red team fools long-hallucination 47%, refund 42%, policy 39%

ideas.name: Word-counter shortcut check before every batch and test
ideas.status: built (scripts/shortcut_check.py); propose as a standing rule
ideas.why: free, seconds; it flags step safety and refund (0.92-0.98) and passes policy (0.64), matching the contrastive results

ideas.name: E23: minimal-pair training data for step safety + refund
ideas.why: same next step / same request under different answers, so one field can't predict the label

ideas.name: 📌 Audit synthetic data for label-overlap bias (reviewer feedback, 2026-10-06)
ideas.why: Do the generators (gpt-oss + DeepSeek) put the right option's words in the text more than the wrong ones'? A skew would teach the word-matching shortcut behind the wording trap. Zero-training check over ~90k examples.
ideas.status: done (D67): our synthetic skills data is below chance for word-matching; public intent data is +0.70

ideas.name: 📌 Flip rate as a standard guard (reviewer feedback)
ideas.why: Wording consistency is measured but wasn't a gate in E22 (0.678 → 0.673). Make the flip rate on the wording eval a guard from docs/NOISE.md.
ideas.status: done (D67): standard guard (GOAL.md, NOISE.md, gate from E23)

ideas.name: 📌 Embedding-space adversarial training for wording (reviewer feedback)
ideas.why: Not E20's twin-consistency loss (killed, D62): perturb option representations adversarially (virtual adversarial training), independent of a fixed wording table. Wording has had 2 attempts (E18, E20) → rule 6: rethink with Shane first.

ideas.name: Process: rules against folly (D65)
ideas.why: Noise-based guards, ≥100-item gate tests, ≤5 guards, prediction, zero-training check first, 2 attempts max. In the template and gate from E22.

ideas.name: Wording robustness, next attempt: many more reworded label sets
ideas.why: E20 killed (D62): agreement learned on ~290 training labels didn't transfer. Reword many diverse label sets (skills-roadmap kinds, sentence-style options) before any loss term. v0.3 goal.

ideas.name: Skills-2 + wording-trap protection (E21 follow-up)
ideas.why: E21 learned the three kinds (0.959; MT-Bench +0.31) but the probe fell 5.7 → 4.7 (D64). Pair the banked skills-2 data with Returns Desk computed-label data (moved the probe on the small model, E12/E13).

ideas.name: Real-data probes: long-answer hallucination, aspect sentiment, stance
ideas.why: Synthetic probes score high (0.89-0.96) but the Decision Index says near zero (RAGTruth 0.00, ACOS 0.02, VAST ~0.07); a real-data probe decides if they're gaps.
ideas.status: done: hallucination +0.14 and stance +0.24 are real gaps; aspect +0.63

ideas.name: Screening 2: 20 more decision kinds
ideas.why: Unscreened candidates on the Decision kinds card (contract clauses, urgency, language, refusal, intent of a query, etc.).
ideas.status: done (2026-10-04): gaps invoice, required elements, refund eligibility, step safety, advice risk

ideas.name: Use the banked skills data (~11.5k)
ideas.why: Test whether 20k skills examples beat 10k, or fold into the next skills batch.

ideas.name: Longer inputs within 8k tokens
ideas.why: 577 Decision Index requests were unsupported (mostly ToolRet's long documents); train on longer states so XL uses its full window.

ideas.name: Abstain precision ≥ 0.90 for the single model
ideas.why: Accuracy mode reached it (0.905, v0.2); the single Kodiak-v0.2-1B is at 0.88. Open v0.3 goal (GOAL.md).
ideas.status: half done: accuracy mode ✓, single model open

ideas.name: Ratings as low / medium / high bands (Stage 3 retry)
ideas.why: Ratings are the weakest answer type; raters disagreed on exact numbers (D31). Test agreement on bands first.

ideas.name: Decision Index engine: sparse attention for long multi-option requests
ideas.why: Engineering, not training: lets the long ToolRet requests run instead of being refused.
ideas.status: paused: no Decision Index runs until Shane says the model is dialed in (2026-10-06)

ideas.name: 'Trick the Bear' game mode
ideas.why: Players try to fool Kodiak; their wins become hard examples (with consent).
